{{Short description|English mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Richard Balam''' ([[Floruit|fl.]] 1653), was an English [[mathematician]].

Balam was the author of ''Algebra, or the Doctrine of composing, inferring, and resolving an Equation'' (1653).<ref>[http://www.enotes.com/topic/Richard_Balam Richard Balam]. eNotes.com. Retrieved March 1st, 2012.</ref> It is a possible source of developments in [[John Wallis]], ''Mathesis Universalis'' (1657), relating to [[geometric progression]]s treated as an [[axiomatic theory]].<ref>{{cite web |url = http://logica.ugent.be/albrecht/thesis/AlgebraRhetoric.pdf |title =The Rhetoric of Problems in Algebra Texbooks from Pacioli to Euler |author = Albrecht Heeffer |date = 2005-10-10 |access-date = 2024-07-13 | pages =27–28}}</ref>
